_purpose: Appendix B hyperparameter table (Aturan Main Fase 5). Every field is either a fixed design fact (verified against source, see 'source' key) or an empirically measured number pulled directly from results/exp05_learning_curve.json (10 independent training seeds) -- none are invented. See rules_spec.md section 12 for the full write-up.
agent: TabularQLearningAgent (src/agents/dqn_agent.py) -- tabular Q-learning, NOT a neural DQN. See rules_spec.md 12.1: no function approximation, no experience replay, no target network anywhere in this codebase.

architecture.type: N/A -- tabular (dict-based Q-table {(features, action): value}), no neural network
architecture.optimizer: N/A -- no gradient-based optimizer; each update is the closed-form tabular Q-learning rule (rules_spec.md Eq. 2)
architecture.batch_size: N/A -- online, one (s,a,r,s') transition updated per call, not minibatched
architecture.replay_buffer_size: N/A -- no replay buffer; on-policy self-play transitions are consumed once via learn_from_episode() at the end of each game, then discarded
architecture.target_network: N/A -- no target network; max_a' Q(s',a') is read from the single live table being updated

update_rule.equation: Q(s,a) <- Q(s,a) + alpha * [ R + gamma * max_a' Q(s',a') - Q(s,a) ]

epsilon.schedule: constant -- no decay over training. This is a known simplification, not fabricated as a schedule that doesn't exist; the older, deprecated QLearningAgent (rules_spec.md 12.2) did decay epsilon (0.9x every 500 games, floor 0.05) but the canonical TabularQLearningAgent does not.

reward_weights_default.note: default reproduces Fase 4 exactly (results/exp04_policy_dependence.json); see results/exp05_reward_sensitivity.json for the swept values and rules_spec.md 12.4/12.6 for the potential-based-shaping discussion

state_discretization.source: src/simulator/agent_env.py AgentGameEnv.observation() -- see rules_spec.md section 12.3 for the full per-field bin table

fields.name: hp_bucket
fields.rule: hp<=35 -> 0, hp<=80 -> 1, hp>80 -> 2 (raw HP, not fraction of own max HP)

fields.name: sasmita_bucket
fields.rule: raw prize count, starts at 3, only decreases

fields.name: num_attacks_affordable
fields.rule: count of currently-affordable attacks, 0-2 (max attacks/character is 2)

fields.name: turn_parity
fields.rule: 1 if this side has initiative this turn

state_discretization.theoretical_max_note: 3*2*2*2*4*4*2*4*3*2 = 18432 (before multiplying by the per-state action dimension); an upper bound assuming every combination is reachable, which it is not -- see empirical table size below and the Balarama hp_bucket=2-unreachable caveat in rules_spec.md 12.3
state_discretization.known_unreachable_case: hp_bucket=2 (hp>80) is structurally unreachable for Balarama (max HP 70, one of Rajasika's two cards) -- verified against data/rajasika.json

empirical_q_table_size.source: results/exp05_learning_curve.json final_table_size, 10 independent training seeds, 3000 self-play games each (SATWIKA vs TAMASIKA, ga_balanced_params.json)
empirical_q_table_size.unit: number of distinct (features, action) keys actually populated in the Q-table after training
empirical_q_table_size.pct_of_theoretical_max_feature_tuples: 6.6% (1222.8 / 18432 unique STATE tuples-equivalent, not directly comparable since this counts (state,action) pairs, but illustrates that only a small fraction of the theoretical state space is ever visited under self-play with this deck pool)

training_regime.total_env_steps_note: one env step = one agent decision (ATTACK or SWITCH); counted directly by train_tabular_agent, not estimated
